g.title: j4259892176
g.text: What can you tell me about the church you and Marie are from, Lyon?

g.title: j1310978788
g.text: Do you consider yourself a religious person, Drifter? Or is this more of a scholarly question?

g.title: j4207975408
g.text: I fear there are many topics I could discuss at length. But do not mistake me, I would be happy to, I simply do not wish to bore you to tears. What where would you like to begin?

g.title: j148058912
g.text: No, I'm more curious than anything else.

g.title: j3901578583
g.text: I'm religious. It's similar to yours, though you wouldn't recognize it.

g.title: j173936918
g.text: I'm religious. You wouldn't recognize any of our practices, though.

g.title: j1795113879
g.text: I'm religious. It's sort of a belief that's personal to me - it doesn't really have a name.

g.title: j326282471
g.text: I follow the path of Sol, like Marie.

g.title: j2469506614
g.text: I'm like you, I follow the path of Lua.

g.title: j1365964957
g.text: I follow the Luminaries, but I try to keep a balanced path.

g.title: j3761817032
g.text: I believe there's something out there, but I don't think people really can know the answers at the end of the day.

g.title: j3245029575
g.text: I'm not religious. I tend to think religion is a crutch of the fearful - no offense.

g.title: j2934998821
g.text: I'm not religious. I won't say there couldn't be something out there, but it's just not something I worry about.

g.title: j3139644957
g.text: I'm not religious. I think all gods - even the Indifference - are a product of our imagination. No offense.

g.title: j4153995921
g.text: Could you tell me about your holidays?

g.title: j267241366
g.text: Could you tell me about Sol and Lua?

g.title: j445428569
g.text: And how did you arrive at such a personal faith, if you do not mind my asking?

g.title: j3522149272
g.text: I wonder how much our faiths influenced each other, intentionally or unintentionally as the case may be.

g.title: j559903528
g.text: Fascinating! As a scholar of the cloth, I do hope we have time to learn from one another at length of our respective beliefs.

g.title: j1016812408
g.text: I studied a bunch of different religions, and none of them really suited me. I wound up with sort of a weird collection of humanity.

g.title: j2067379145
g.text: I believe what I feel. And I don't need a building or a book to tell me what that is.

g.title: j2937496477
g.text: Truly? I am... surprised. Surprised, but pleased. And it is no wonder you are curious, then. Our teachings must be so very foreign to what you know. So much time has passed.

g.title: j2923713148
g.text: I respect that. There is honor in recognizing what we cannot know, in seeing the smallness of the human condition.

g.title: j1757294285
g.text: Believe you me, there is no offence taken. In many cases, you are quite correct.

g.title: j2111426692
g.text: I would admit I am jealous that you do not find cause to fret over what may wait for us beyond the veil. Would that more others did, our world would have known more peace in its days.

g.title: j2351138878
g.text: That is a topic over which I wish to talk with you at great length. Simply not now, at a time when I am not prepared for such a discussion.

g.title: j2176586754
g.text: A wise place to begin. To know a culture by its holidays is to know its heart. For how a people celebrates is how they would be remembered. For those moments are the ones cherished most by those who share them.

g.title: j3913820152
g.text: Of course. Let us begin with that which you may already know: Sol and Lua, the sun and the moon. They are deities who are forever transmutable in their aspects.

g.title: j3946888082
g.text: Hm. Allow me to answer your curiosity. In order to avoid boring you to tears, where would you like to begin?

g.title: j2351723904
g.text: And I am remiss in not staying on topic. I fear I have wandered far from the topic at hand.

g.title: j3240965408
g.text: It doesn't mean I'm not interested in learning, however.

g.title: j3090646825
g.text: Our main and most common holidays are the Winter and Summer Solstices that mark the shortest and longest days of the year.

g.title: j3477967620
g.text: Appearing in many forms over the centuries to many believers. Sometimes male, sometimes female. But always as Sol, the Sun, and Lua, the Moon.

g.title: j593607843
g.text: You wished to know about the Luminary Orthodoxy, did you not? In order to avoid boring you to tears, where would you like to begin?

g.title: j502149487
g.text: Mm. And one best told to a trusted friend. I understand completely. Besides which, you came to me for information, not the other way around.

g.title: j4055165688
g.text: A stained glass window of the soul. Shattered when left apart, but what a beautiful image it paints when assembled.

g.title: j446086654
g.text: The world would be a better place, if it shared your faith.

g.title: j800731109
g.text: And for that, I laud your curiosity and scholarly nature.

g.title: j2861361973
g.text: My case is... complex. But I will not lie and say that it has not been devoid of fear. Though religion has brought a flood of it into my life. It has never removed it.

g.title: j1006894806
g.text: Both holidays are marked by great feasts, though they are delineated by whom you share the feasts with. Where the Winter Solstice is for sharing with family and close friends, the Summer Solstice is for strangers.

g.title: j2825650989
g.text: Oh, that makes so much more sense now.

g.title: j2269184308
g.text: Really? Tell me more about the Summer Solstice.

g.title: j2344142190
g.text: Tell me more about the Winter Solstice.

g.title: j548800671
g.text: Yes, some sects can be a bit strict in their choice of iconography, declaring that Sol "Must" be one way or "Must" be another but the Orthodoxy does not recognize this as fact.

g.title: j909654574
g.text: Each of the Luminaries holds within them multiple aspects. Each aspect can be seen as a function of the whole. Lua, for example, is the mother, the maiden, the crone.

g.title: j1291961447
g.text: The Summer Solstice is for sharing great bounties and for bringing together strangers who have never met. You would gather in a field, bringing food and wares of your own making, it would not matter what.

g.title: j684431399
g.text: The Winter Solstice is for bracing against the cold and cherishing those who warm us against the darkest times. You decorate a tree with candles, one light for each of those who have gone before who guide the way as the stars in the sky.

g.title: j2958288033
g.text: I expect that whatever has survived to this far-flung future has wound up being... a bit confused in its documentation of my religion.

g.title: j3731378977
g.text: But Lua can also be He who guides souls along the river of tears to the endless night. Death himself. The harbinger and herald.

g.title: j2896618745
g.text: Candles, or bread, or clothes, or paintings. Or books of poetry. Or wreaths of flowers. Even to come empty handed but "with glad tidings" is to be seen as a blessing.

g.title: j1389574110
g.text: And atop it, Sol himself, suffering atop the star tree in the darkness. Dimmed, but not forgotten. For this is the time of Lua. And we celebrate her in this time of shadow.

g.title: j3344825619
g.text: I find myself a living archaeological relic. How depressing. But I digress.

g.title: j2027385197
g.text: And in other sects, Death is an old veiled woman. It differs. But it speaks to the same spirit reaching out to all of us. The silvered hand that wishes to guide us in that last moment.

g.title: j52566173
g.text: A celebration of life - laughter - music - sharing of all of these things, would commence during that, the longest of Sol's days.

g.title: j333093705
g.text: And as we draw in close, and we feast upon a roasted bird and root vegetables and all that does not grow fresh in the frozen earth, we hold those that we love. And we tell stories of those that have gone.

g.title: j4139900077
g.text: The moon that slips over the sun during the eclipse, guiding us through the crossroads in that moment where all is lost.

g.title: j3131215254
g.text: All were welcome to make new friends of strangers, and take home that which they needed.

g.title: j3210860494
g.text: We remember, on Lua's longest night, that she will guide us and our family through in the end.

g.title: j650819662
g.text: But the most sacred of holidays to the Luminaries is The Summum Bonum. It is a rare event, when Sol and Lua align into a perfect eclipse.

g.title: j88202600
g.text: It is a wonderous and holy occasion, where all of nature responds. Have you had such luck as to witness it yourself?

g.title: j164384313
g.text: Have you ever seen an eclipse yourself?

g.title: j2381071396
g.text: I have been blessed to witness it twice. And both times, I found it... transformative. If I could stay within that brief moment, suspended there forever, I would.

g.title: j239204383
g.text: I will tell you the story of the first eclipse I witnessed another time. It has grown late here. Or perhaps it is early. I cannot quite tell.

g.title: j548523390
g.text: I have. It wasn't that impressive.

g.title: j4181351423
g.text: I have. It gave me a horrible ocular megrim, believe it or not. But it was amazing.

g.title: j3336502689
g.text: I have. It gave me a horrible ocular migraine, believe it or not. But it was amazing.

g.title: j1001114438
g.text: Does this phrase sound familiar to you: "On empty crossroads, seek the eclipse - for when Sol and Lua align, the lost shall find their way home."

g.title: j1390764445
g.text: If you ever have the opportunity, do so.

g.title: j2226631914
g.text: Would that I could share your impassiveness over the event...

g.title: j142588219
g.text: You must be touched by the Luminaries, and their presence overwhelmed you. Or perhaps they wished to smite you for some great sin. One or the other. Heh.

g.title: j3378445911
g.text: Celestines 18:19, from the Third Orthodox Book of Lua. Where in the name of the Luminaries did you hear it?

g.title: j1824009834
g.text: I look forward to it. Thanks for taking the time, Lyon.

g.title: j1712711487
g.text: Such is the way of the gods. Their signs can often be interpreted any which way.

g.title: j2858974317
g.text: It's a very long story. But needless to say, I think some of your scripture is now running around with the Indifference.

g.title: j2419829538
g.text: From some old friends. They were using it as two halves of a spy phrase with their daughter who... never mind, actually.

g.title: j1508250116
g.text: It involves the Man in the Wall and it's all very messy.

g.title: j666696255
g.text: Yes, well. It... is beginning to seem inevitable.

g.title: j3113627502
g.text: I... see. I would like to ask you more about this soon, if I may. I simply am not prepared for this now, and it has grown late here. Or perhaps it is early. I cannot quite tell.

g.title: j1612995700
g.text: I look forward to it. Thanks for taking the time, Lyon.

g.title: j450941103
g.text: Yes, well. It... is beginning to seem inevitable.
